acceptance_criteria: Deep dependency graphs resolve without recursion failure
Completed work scores zero and relays no boost

items.title: v0.1.2 - Apply ergonomics
items.description: First use of the kit on its own backlog showed that apply succeeds but does not explain itself: a failure names no item, and a completed scaffold can still leave the target unconverged.
acceptance_criteria: An apply failure names the item, the field, and the reason
One scaffold apply converges a fresh Project

items.title: v0.2.0 - GitHub operational authority
items.description: Let fresh GitHub operational state govern existing work instead of stale local intent. Policy D1 and carryover policy A are approved.
acceptance_criteria: Remote completion and assignment survive ordinary sync
Sprint commitments and carryover are explicit and reviewed

items.title: v0.3.0 - Adoption

acceptance_criteria: An existing repository can be imported without touching unselected issues

items.title: v0.4.0+ - Reconciliation and reach
items.description: Close the reconciliation gaps and settle the transport question.
acceptance_criteria: Removal and reverse-sync have explicit policy, preview, and recovery
The dedicated-MCP decision is recorded with evidence

items.title: Infer hierarchy and dependencies when importing existing issues
items.description:
Import (R11) adopts an existing issue with a neutral type, no parent and no dependencies.

GitHub already records sub-issue links and `blocked_by` dependencies for these issues, so an import preview could propose that structure rather than flattening it. It does not yet: every adopted item lands with `parent: null` and `depends_on: []`, and a human has to rebuild the shape by hand.

Reading it costs one extra request per issue for the parent and one for dependencies, which is why the first cut left it out. Worth revisiting once import has been used on a repository big enough to care.

Found while implementing R11 on 2026-09-19.

items.title: Make the Agentic Backlog Kit a finished product
items.description: Take the kit from a shipped v0.1.0 that only its author can use to a product another team can adopt on an existing repository.
acceptance_criteria: Every release line has an owner, a denominator, and a done definition
The kit manages its own backlog through its own workflows

items.title: R01 - Bind apply operations to fresh local and remote state
items.description: Sync, scaffold, and bootstrap plans bind normalized local and remote fingerprints with per-action preconditions, and apply aborts on drift.
acceptance_criteria: Drift aborts before the first write
Partial failure produces an auditable receipt

items.title: R02 - Run live GitHub end-to-end evaluations

acceptance_criteria: Each supported executor completes the workflow

items.title: R03 - Complete first-run Project creation and discovery

acceptance_criteria: A user can start with only an organization and repository

items.title: R04 - Reconcile complete Project view configuration

acceptance_criteria: Incorrect same-name views are detected and repair plans converge

items.title: R05 - Manage the iteration lifecycle

items.title: R06 - Evaluate the installed plugin and skill activation

CI detects material output-size regressions

items.title: R10 - Add destructive and reverse reconciliation
items.description: Synchronization is deliberately additive and update-only: it does not close deleted work, remove obsolete parents, archive Project items, or reconcile remote-only changes back into local intent.
acceptance_criteria: Every removal has explicit policy, preview, confirmation, audit, and recovery

items.title: R11 - Import existing backlogs and support bulk ingestion
items.description: Ingestion handles one structured item at a time and only marked issues are managed, so the kit is usable only on a greenfield repository. This is the gate on adoption by anyone other than the maintainer.
acceptance_criteria: An existing repository imports without modifying unselected issues
Duplicate mappings are rejected
A second import is idempotent

items.title: R12 - Support multi-repository portfolio planning

acceptance_criteria: Multiple repositories participate in one portfolio without ID ambiguity

items.title: R13 - Complete native transport parity and decide on a dedicated MCP server
items.description: Authenticated gh and direct GraphQL are proven peers. The installed generic GitHub MCP lacks the Projects surface and fails capability preflight without writing.
acceptance_criteria: Every declared-compatible route produces equivalent plans and state

items.title: R14 - Adopt organization-managed semantic releases
items.description: Version calculation, tagging, and Release creation are delegated to the reusable workflows in aegolius-labs/.github. Hosted no-bump and immutable publication passed; missing-baseline handling and recovery proof remain.
acceptance_criteria: The shared interface and caller pass permission and recovery tests
Hosted failure recovery after draft creation is proven

items.title: R15 - Respect GitHub operational status and sprint authority
items.description: Ordinary sync overwrites remote Status and Sprint with stale local intent, so remote completion and assignment are lost. Policy D1 is approved: fresh GitHub state governs existing work.
acceptance_criteria: Remote completion and assignment survive stale local intent
Planning uses fresh operational state
Explicit transitions fail safely on drift

items.title: R16 - Preserve sprint commitments and review carryover
items.description: Replanning must not move committed work automatically or regress status. Carryover policy A is approved: work assigned elsewhere is excluded from automatic selection and offered as explicit carryover.
acceptance_criteria: Replanning neither moves work automatically nor regresses status
Capacity, dependencies, overage, and carryover verify against fresh state

items.title: R17 - Support deep dependency graphs without recursion failure
items.description: Prioritization raised RecursionError from roughly 500 chained items and validation from roughly 1,200. Both traversals are now iterative and cycle diagnostics are bounded.
acceptance_criteria: 10,000-node forward and reverse chains validate and prioritize
Deep cycles are still detected and reported compactly
The benchmark report digest is unchanged

items.title: R18 - Enforce zero final scores for completed work
items.description: The dependency boost propagated into the final score of completed work, so a Done item with two dependents scored 4.0 instead of 0.0 and relayed a boost to its own prerequisites.
acceptance_criteria: Completed prerequisites score zero for default and custom done statuses
Unfinished graph scores and stable ordering are unchanged

items.title: R19 - Publish accurate release and remediation status
items.description: Public main documents the completed v0.1.0 release and the outstanding corrective work. Verified present on origin/main on 2026-09-18.
acceptance_criteria: Public main documents the release and outstanding work

items.title: R20 - Resolve remaining disposable evaluation resources
items.description: Cleanup stopped safely on its first repository-deletion failure. Project #4 is deleted, its private repository remains, and the API Project #5 and repository were untouched. No deletion is authorized yet.
acceptance_criteria: Remaining resources are verified absent or retention is elected

items.title: R21 - Run the kit against its own backlog
items.description: The kit had never been pointed at its own work: zero issues, no manifest, no managed Project. This roadmap was maintained by hand in one large Markdown file - exactly the artifact the kit exists to manage.
acceptance_criteria: A tracked manifest describes the open roadmap
A scaffolded Project reflects it
A second sync plan contains zero actions
Friction is written up against the responsible work item

items.title: R22 - Report actionable apply failures
items.description: An apply failure surfaces as 'GitHub API error 1: gh: Validation Failed (HTTP 422)', naming no item, field or reason. Diagnosis required reading the receipt, querying organization issue types by hand, and reading the transport source. The receipt is good; the operator-facing message is not.
acceptance_criteria: A failed action names the item id and the rejected field
A known cause such as an unavailable issue type is named explicitly
The remedy or the fallback taken is stated

items.title: R23 - Converge a fresh Project in one scaffold apply
items.description: project.view.create cannot carry a filter, visible fields, grouping or sorting, so every created view needs an immediate repair pass. The first apply reports completed with 17 of 17 actions while leaving three views unconverged; convergence arrives only on the third plan.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh Project converges in one reviewed apply, or the plan states plainly that a second pass is required
A completed status never implies a converged target when it is not

items.title: R24 - Reconsider hierarchy expressiveness for small work
items.description: The hierarchy is a strict ladder and a parent must be exactly one level above its child, so a small chore directly under a Feature has no type: Task is reserved for level 5 under a Story or Bug. Six decomposed items had to be retyped from Task to Story, which overstates them. This may be intentional; it is recorded rather than scheduled.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded either way, with the modeling rationale

items.title: R25 - Carry a canonical GUID through to GitHub for Seam A traceability
items.description:
The authority model in aio-agentic-sdlc requires that a canonical GUID be carried into the ABK item and into the GitHub issue body marker, so a projected issue can always be traced back to its Intention DAG node. This kit cannot do that. `$defs.item` in schemas/manifest.schema.json sets `additionalProperties: false` over a fixed fourteen-field list with no GUID field, so an item carrying one fails validation. The marker is `<!-- agentic-backlog-kit:id=<id>;schema=1 -->`; the separator leaves room for a second key but nothing writes or reads one.

Seam B (agentic-qa-kit to here) is implemented and pinned by fixtures on both sides. Seam A is documented and unbuilt: neither repository references the other in src or tests.

This does not block standalone use, which is a supported configuration, not a degraded one. It is a cost that grows. Adding the carrier later means a schema version bump, a marker extension, and a re-link pass over every issue created before it. That is cheap at fifty issues and expensive at five thousand, which is why it is recorded now rather than when the framework arrives.

Found on 2026-09-21 while assessing whether aio-agentic-sdlc can be adopted after this kit is already in use.
acceptance_criteria: A manifest item can carry an optional canonical GUID without failing validation, under a bumped schema version with a tested migration from version 1
The issue body marker carries the GUID when the item has one, and round-trips through read and adoption without loss
An item with no GUID stays valid, because standalone use owns no Intention DAG
A Seam A fixture is committed here and its counterpart in aio-agentic-sdlc, so neither repository imports the other to test the contract

items.title: Preview unmanaged issues read-only
items.description: A read-only import preview lists unmanaged issues with inferred types and relationships, touching nothing.
acceptance_criteria: The preview performs no writes
Unselected issues are never modified

items.title: Assign stable IDs and apply adoption in deterministic batches
items.description: Reviewed mappings receive stable local IDs and are adopted in deterministic batches.
acceptance_criteria: Duplicate mappings are rejected
A second import is idempotent

items.title: Cover adoption in the skills, not only the CLI
items.description:
The skills directory carries backlog-init, backlog-ingest, backlog-prioritize, backlog-sprint-plan and backlog-sync-github, and none of them mentions adoption. R11 and the relationship inference that followed it are reachable from the CLI and from docs/importing.md only.

That inverts the adoption story. An agent working through the installed plugin can initialize a backlog and synchronize one it already manages, but cannot take on a repository that already has issues, which is the path any new user is actually on. Ingestion handles one structured item at a time, so without an adoption skill the plugin's answer to an existing backlog is to re-file it by hand.

Found on 2026-09-21 while assessing readiness for use across existing projects.
acceptance_criteria: A skill covers the plan, review, apply and reconcile shape of adoption, including what adoption writes and what it leaves alone
It states that relationship inference is opt-in and why, and what a withheld relationship means
It routes orphan recovery to import-reconcile rather than to a second adoption
Skill structural validation and host manifest parity stay green

items.title: Enforce the release baseline prerequisite without auto-tagging
items.description: Untagged release-bearing history silently analyzed zero commits before baseline setup (R14-F7). The prerequisite must be explicit and must not create a tag on its own.
acceptance_criteria: A missing baseline fails loudly
No tag is created automatically

acceptance_criteria: A hosted run recovers from a partial asset upload

items.title: Compose fresh operational state for planning

acceptance_criteria: Planning inputs come from fresh remote state
Offline preview limits are documented

items.title: Preserve remote Status and Sprint during ordinary sync

items.title: Represent operational changes as explicit digest-bound transitions

acceptance_criteria: A transition aborts when remote state moved since planning

items.title: Document legacy-manifest migration

acceptance_criteria: Migration guidance covers manifests written before D1

acceptance_criteria: Replanning does not double-count retained work

items.title: Offer explicit carryover review for work assigned elsewhere

acceptance_criteria: Remaining resources are enumerated from fresh discovery

items.title: Express the roadmap as a tracked manifest

acceptance_criteria: The manifest validates

items.title: Write up first-use friction against the responsible item

acceptance_criteria: Each observation names the item that owns it

items.title: Name the item and rejected field on apply failure

items.title: Explain an unavailable native issue type

acceptance_criteria: A missing native type is named
